items.title: Fibres of the henselization of the normalization and the minimal primes over a local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local ring A with finitely many minimal primes, lets A' be the integral closure of A in the total ring of fractions of A_red, and considers the two maps Spec(A') <- Spec((A')^h) -> Spec(A^h) attached to the henselization, where (A')^h = A' tensor_A A^h; it asserts that the left arrow is bijective on maximal ideals, that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes, and that every minimal prime of (A')^h lies in a unique maximal ideal while every maximal ideal contains exactly one minimal prime (source lines 31154-31171). The proof runs the same three-part programme as the strict-henselization analogue counted separately: removal of nilpotents using (A/I)^h = A^h/IA^h, a computation identifying the fibres of the left arrow with spectra of residue field tensor products in the finite henselian case, the use of normality of the filtered colimit (A')^h to get uniqueness of the minimal prime inside each maximal ideal together with a henselian-pair connectedness argument for the converse, and a two-sided comparison of minimal primes via the total fraction ring. The arguments are independent of the geometric variant, which uses strict henselization and a separable algebraic closure and is counted at disjoint lines.
